name: Game logic stays testable without the browser
instruction: Game state changes live in exported plain functions that do not depend on canvas, DOM APIs, or animation frames.
relevant_when: A TypeScript file under src/games/<game-id>/game.ts that defines game state, scoring, movement, hit detection, input actions, or round progression for a CarnivalGame.
context: AGENTS.md says game logic is testable without a browser: state changes such as scoring, moving, and hits stay in plain exported functions and only start touches the canvas, the DOM, or requestAnimationFrame.
scope_reason: A game.ts file shows which functions own state changes and whether those functions are exported and free of browser-only APIs.

checklist.name: exports-state-logic
checklist.rule: Core state-changing game logic, such as createState, step, scoring, hit detection, movement, or player actions, is implemented in exported functions or exported types that tests can import directly.

checklist.name: logic-avoids-browser-apis
checklist.rule: Those exported logic functions do not use CanvasRenderingContext2D, HTMLElement, document, window, localStorage, addEventListener, requestAnimationFrame, or pointer/keyboard event objects; browser-only APIs stay in start or drawing code.
